import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Quick correlation check for top features
    # Use only top 20 features by t-statistic
    t_stats = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y==0, i]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y==1, i]
        t, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
        t_stats.append((abs(t), fid))
    
    t_stats.sort(reverse=True)
    top_features = [fid for _, fid in t_stats[:20]]
    
    # Check for product terms among top features
    best_product = None
    best_t = 0
    
    # Only test a subset of pairs to speed up
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(top_features[:10]):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(top_features[i+1:15], i+1):
            # Skip near-duplicates
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,feats.column(fid1)], feats.x[:,feats.column(fid2)])[0,1]) >= 0.6:
                continue
                
            # Create product feature
            col1 = feats.column(fid1)
            col2 = feats.column(fid2)
            prod = feats.x[:,col1] * feats.x[:,col2]
            
            # Test association with outcome
            t, _ = stats.ttest_ind(prod[feats.y==0], prod[feats.y==1], equal_var=False)
            if abs(t) > best_t:
                best_t = abs(t)
                best_product = (fid1, fid2)
    
    if not best_product or best_t < 2.5:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Return best product term
    fid1, fid2 = best_product
    return Design(
        drivers=(fid1, fid2),
        columns=(fid1, fid2),
        products=((fid1, fid2),),
        loadings={fid1: 0.5, fid2: 0.5}
    )
